chapter: Henderson, Lester and the bands breaking up
title: Fletcher Henderson's wife playing Hawkins records for Lester
summary: Lester recalls having to listen to Hawkins records at the Hendersons' house.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: He says, "I sure will." So he says -- you know, he always dug Prez, man. And Prez told me, he says, "Buddy," -- this is like after I joined the band -- he says, "I stayed with him." Fletcher had a nice house on 139th Street. And he says, -- Fletcher's wife would take him downstairs and put on Hawk's records. He says, "Listen to this." Says, "This is what's happening, baby." Of course, they didn't use that saying then, but, "This is the way you're supposed to sound." He said, "Can't you sound like that?" And he says, "Of course, I had to be refined. I couldn't call her the bitch as I wanted to call her."
He says, "You know, she was an ex-circus trumpet-playing bitch." You know who she was? She had been married to Fletcher's trumpet player first, to Russell.

Russell Smith. So when -- so he married Russell's wife, see? So then Russell had taught her to play trumpet, so she was a little trumpet player. Said, "I hated that bitch." Said, "She taken me downstairs every morning and put that -- you know. And I'm staying in her house," said, "I had to play my little banjo."
